Container.Name: Lodestar
Container.Overview: Lodestar crawls the BitTorrent DHT, fetches torrent metadata from peers and makes it searchable. It keeps names, file lists, sizes, dates and swarm counts in one local index. Open the web UI after the first start. The setup token appears in the container log. Enter it to create the admin password.

Config.Name: DHT / peers (UDP)
Config.Description: DHT traffic. Forward this UDP port on your router for best reach.

Config.Name: Peers (TCP)
Config.Description: Reserved for incoming peer connections (planned). Lodestar only makes outbound fetches today, so nothing listens here yet.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Index, database and settings. Use a pool path (/mnt/cache/... or your pool name), not /mnt/user. /mnt/user goes through Unraid's FUSE layer, which is slow for this workload and risky for SQLite.

Config.Name: Hot path (optional)
Config.Description: Planned, not used yet. Optional. Indexes and hot columns. Must be on an SSD or NVMe pool. Leave empty to keep everything under Data.

Config.Name: Cold path (optional)
Config.Description: Planned, not used yet. Optional. File-tree blobs and the optional raw archive. Written continuously as torrents arrive, so on the parity array it keeps disks spinning and slows writes. Keep it on the cache pool unless you have a reason.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: The user Lodestar runs as. Leave it at 99 (nobody), the safe Unraid default. Lodestar makes the Data folder belong to this user on start. Never use 0: that is root, which is unsafe, and Lodestar refuses it.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: The group Lodestar runs as. Leave it at 100 (users), the safe Unraid default. Never use 0: that is the root group, which is unsafe.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Time zone for log timestamps, for example Europe/Berlin.

Config.Name: Intensity
Config.Description: How hard the crawler works: low, balanced or aggressive. Balanced opens about 400 metadata connections at once. Aggressive opens about 1000, and some home routers cannot track that many.
